name: Ho Chi Minh Thought
summary: Ho Chi Minh Thought is the Communist Party of Vietnam's official ideology, combining Marxism-Leninism with Vietnamese national liberation. It treats independence, national unity and socialism as one project led by the Party, with the peasantry and the working class as its base. It stresses a state of the people, a strong state sector, anti-colonialism and an ethic of frugal, selfless service by cadres.
scope: The profile represents Ho's own writings and speeches (1920s to 1960s) and the policy of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam in his lifetime, including his Fifth Comintern report (1924), the 1945 Declaration of Independence and his 1956 article on ideological unity, drawing on the CPV's 1991 formalization only where it codifies those ideas. It excludes the post-1991 socialist-oriented market line of Doi Moi and Western or dissident readings.

sources.usedFor: Official CPV formulation: independence and unity, Party role, state sector, morality, people as masters, dictatorship of the proletariat.

sources.usedFor: Peasants, land, colonial exploitation, revolution and Comintern duties.

sources.title: Vietnamese Declaration of Independence (1945)
sources.author: Ho Chi Minh
sources.usedFor: Equality of peoples, self-determination, end of monarchy, popular authority.

sources.title: Consolidation and Development of Ideological Unity Among Marxist-Leninist Parties (1956)
sources.author: Ho Chi Minh
sources.usedFor: National roads to socialism, internationalism, party discipline, Soviet camp, cult of personality.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a theme in the sources, but socialism is described as improving the material and spiritual life of the people, and the DRV built state health services; inferred from that aim.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is not addressed; an adherent would favour better pay for workers as part of socialist distribution by labor, inferred rather than stated.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ideology calls for a leading state sector as the material basis of socialism, though it tolerated non-socialist economic factors during transition, so a clear disagreement but not absolute.

public-ownership.rationale: The state sector is seen as essential and Ho is quoted calling for its development to create the material basis for socialism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not discussed directly; socialist aims of fair, equal social relations imply heavier burdens on the rich, but inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Workers' organizations are part of the united worker front under Party leadership; unions are valued as Party-led bodies, not as independent bargainers.

property-fundamental.rationale: Socialism requires workers' ownership of the means of production; private property is tolerated in transition but not treated as a near-inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations are not a focus; state direction of the economy implies tight control of private firms, inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Aim of improving people's material life and equality makes welfare cuts unattractive, but welfare policy was not specifically treated.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialism is described as workers' ownership of the means of production, though in practice via state and cooperative forms rather than firm-by-firm ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security of the Party-state against enemies ranks high; inferred from one-party security practice, not stated for terrorism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Strong stress on revolutionary morality, thrift and self-discipline suggests opposition; drugs were not addressed directly.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Declaration condemns racial oppression and the ideology values equality among peoples; legal restriction of speech fits Party control but is inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Collective leadership under the Party is stressed rather than a leader bypassing institutions, yet Ho himself was a revered leader; adherents are mixed.

state-harmful.rationale: The goal is a true state of the people, by the people, for the people, and the state is kept strong; the claim is flatly opposed.

limit-guns.rationale: Revolution relies on armed people's forces under Party control, so civilian arms are subordinate to the state; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: National defense by all the people and building people's armed forces are core tasks of the ideology.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Ho's morality stresses integrity and public-spiritedness and socialist Vietnam criminalized it; inferred, not stated.

decide-locally.rationale: National unity and a centralized Party-led state are core, with democratic centralism rather than local autonomy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Reeducation and moral remolding are consistent with revolutionary humanism, though not documented in the sources opened.

traditional-family.rationale: Ho drew on Confucian virtues but criticized Confucian ethics; the Party also promotes women's equality, so adherents are mixed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The ideology never addressed it; official Marxist-Leninist Vietnam long did not recognize it, so a mild inferred disagreement.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; socialist Vietnam legalized abortion, inferred from state practice and women's equality.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ho respected Christianity, Buddhism and Confucian good sides, but the Party is atheist and wants a secular public sphere; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Ho condemned racial hatred and colonial oppression of all races and called for equality, though remedy policies were not discussed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; Marxism-Leninism treats women's subordination as social, but no explicit position from Ho Chi Minh Thought.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The ideology draws on traditional Vietnamese culture and ties national independence to cultural development.

gradual-change.rationale: Ho championed revolution, while the transition to socialism is described as gradual, so the statement's institutional deference is rejected.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; no basis to take a side.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Ho valued socialist-camp solidarity and peaceful coexistence but never argued for empowering bodies like the UN; split and inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Development of a state-led economy as the material base of socialism suggests skepticism, but trade was not directly treated.

nation-first.rationale: Ho held that genuine patriotism cannot be separated from proletarian internationalism, which cuts both ways on this item.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Opposition to imperialist aggression and emphasis on national sovereignty make adherents wary of interventions abroad; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: National independence and unity are foundational; open borders sit poorly with them, though a communist world is the distant aim.

limit-growth.rationale: Socialism needs a highly developed productive base, so growth limits conflict with the program.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology and anachronistic; no basis for a firm position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Building a developed productive base is the route to socialism, implying faith in science and technology, inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Ho called colonial peoples ripe for insurrection and urged Communist help to revolution and liberation.

experts-over-public.rationale: The state is meant to be of and for the people, but intellectuals work within Party leadership; mild inferred disagreement.

central-planning.rationale: The state sector is central to building socialism, but the ideology allowed mixed forms during transition, so not strongest.

socialized-markets.rationale: Non-socialist and socialist factors coexist in the transition under state leadership, inferred to allow markets under public control.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; no basis for a position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Equality and workers' ownership imply taxing large inheritances, but this was not directly discussed.

basic-income.rationale: Distribution is by labor in socialism's first stage, which conflicts with unconditional income; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The state-led building of an independent economic base implies protection of domestic industry, inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state sector is to build the material basis for socialism, which means directing investment to strategic sectors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Aims are workers' ownership and a leading state sector, though peasant smallholding was tolerated; the statement is not the goal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Distribution by labor is the socialist stage, with money and wages ending only in distant communism; adherents defer the question.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A state-directed economy implies strong state financial institutions; abolition for market money is opposed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Workers and employers are not conceived as partners; social organization runs through Party-led fronts instead.

one-party-rule.rationale: The CPV is the center of the revolution, and Marxism-Leninism with Ho Chi Minh Thought is its ideological basis.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Declaration celebrates the overthrow of the monarchy and founding of a democratic republic.

democracy-best.rationale: Ho spoke of people being masters and a democratic regime, but within Party leadership and not liberal-democratic majoritarianism; split reading.

direct-votes.rationale: Democracy is exercised through the Party-led state and fronts rather than direct referenda; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power is held by the Party-led state; soviet-style councils were not the basis.

right-to-secede.rationale: National unity and independence are foundational and the Party is the core of national liberation, so secession is rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equality of all peoples from birth is proclaimed, rejecting natural rulers, though Party cadres are expected to lead.

political-violence-never.rationale: In his 1924 Comintern report Ho called the colonial peasants 'ripe for insurrection' and said the International must help them to revolution and liberation.

war-builds-character.rationale: The ideology fights wars of liberation but frames war as a regrettable necessity; not a character builder either way.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Party is secular and keeps religion apart from the state, though Ho spoke respectfully of religions; moderate inference.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Implied by the Marxist-Leninist basis of the state, whose laws come from the Party and people; scripture-based law is not discussed.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Implied by the doctrine of national defense of all people under the state and Party; private security and courts are never discussed.

military-superiority.rationale: National defense by all the people is central, but superiority over rivals as a goal was not stated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Vietnam is a multiethnic state; Ho's 1955 letter addressed ethnic minorities as equal members, but a single nation is the goal.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is the foundation and class liberation is a core element, but Ho put national liberation first in colonial conditions, so class conflict is not the sole engine of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialist society should have healthy, fair and equal social relations with no gap between mental and manual labor or town and country.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; ethnic minorities were granted autonomous regions, but sovereignty of land remains with the state.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Declaration lists French theft of land and resources, supporting redress, but reparations as such were not claimed.

civilizational-union.rationale: The union Ho promoted is of socialist parties across civilizations, not religion-based union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ho wrote against individualism and taught selflessness and public-spiritedness.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Revolutionary ethics stress devotion to the collective and cadres as servants; the Declaration also cites universal rights, so a moderate yes.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed in the documents opened; policy shifted over time.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The ideology aims at developing industrial productive forces; calling it a disaster contradicts that.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Development is wanted, but disrupting institutions is not; split and inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The Party-state values security and control; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Ho's program is revolutionary change toward socialism and liberation, the opposite of restoring a past order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is the guiding ideology of policy, though Ho adapted it to conditions; ideology is prior to results.

direct-action.rationale: Revolution is organized by a disciplined party; Ho did not ground change in decentralized direct action, but he also used elections and insurrection.

means-match-ends.rationale: Ho held that revolutionary violence is necessary but stressed moral conduct; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Implied by the program of building the material and technical basis of socialism; a hunter-gatherer life is never considered.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Ho wanted no opposition between mental and manual labor in the long run, but no immediate abolition; split.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by labor under socialism, with need-based distribution at the communist stage as the final goal.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialism is meant to raise the material and spiritual life of the people rather than serve profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Ho described colonial peoples as exploited by imperialist capital, in line with Marxist theory of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought describes a dictatorship of the proletariat built on unity of workers, peasants and intellectuals under Party leadership.

collective-farming.rationale: The path was land reform to small farmers then cooperatives; collectivization came later and adherents split on timing.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Ho followed Lenin's analysis of imperialism, which holds that capitalism produces colonial wars.

taxation-theft.rationale: Implied by the leading role of the state sector in building socialism; the libertarian view of tax as theft is not discussed.

harm-principle.rationale: The state shapes culture, ethics and economy; a narrow harm limit is not held.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Ho attacked individualism and emphasized the collective; though he cited individual rights in the Declaration, rights belonging only to individuals is rejected.

conscription.rationale: National defense by all the people and people's armed forces support conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the doctrine's stress on national unity and the people as masters of the state.

state-as-business.rationale: Implied by the view of the state as the people's own, with cadres as their servants; managerial business models of government are not discussed.

positive-liberty.rationale: Socialism aims to improve people's material and spiritual life so they can truly be free, matching the material-means conception.

media-academia-power.rationale: The ideology sees capitalists and imperialists as holding power, not media and universities; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Declaration declares that all peoples are equal from birth, and Ho attacked racial hatred.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation runs through the Party and fronts of classes, not families and trade bodies as organic estates.

total-state.rationale: The state leads economy, culture and education under the Party, but Ho spoke of the state of the people and not of total control; split.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ho called for national revival after colonial humiliation, but not decadence-and-rebirth rhetoric of fascism; moderately inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The ideology is anti-imperialist and focused on liberation; expansion contradicts it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Ho rejected feudal monarchy and founded a republic on popular sovereignty.

bound-labor.rationale: Ho denounced colonial policy turning peasants into serfs bound to the land.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds ideology reflects class interests, but Ho did not take up the epistemic claim; split.

universal-morality.rationale: Ho stressed revolutionary morality but grounded it in class and nation as well as universal values; split.

single-common-good.rationale: The Party claims to represent the whole people and one national interest, though class lines remain; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

revive-national-language.rationale: Vietnamese was already the national language; the question did not arise.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' ownership and the people as masters imply worker participation in running enterprises, though under Party guidance.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is a state and Party responsibility, so private-choice vouchers are opposed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: State-led development does not fear deficits per se; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: The ideology holds that political liberation requires socialism and does not tie it to private economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Party members are taught to exemplify Ho's personal values and cadres to serve as models, but the sources do not set example above law, and Ho also built a constitutional state from 1946.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Declaration invokes the principles of self-determination and equality of nations and claims Vietnam's right to be free and independent.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; Ho's Vietnam fought wars of national defense and liberation, not discretionary force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is rationalist and Ho respected the good in religions; split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Distribution by labor is the socialist principle and Ho praised industriousness, inferred as consistent.

class-collaboration.rationale: Ho described workers and peasants exploited by capital and landlords, though the national front united classes including patriotic capitalists; mixed but leaning no.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Implied by the doctrine's roots in Vietnamese tradition, Confucianism and Buddhism; destroying cultural institutions is not discussed.

dominated-front.rationale: Ho urged colonial peoples to unite and the International to help them against imperialism.

workers-nation.rationale: Ho held that patriotism cannot be separated from proletarian internationalism, rejecting a purely national working class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Party advocated women's equality; Ho wrote of women's oppression under colonialism; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Declaration asserts equality of all peoples from birth; Ho condemned racial hatred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds the state as a class instrument, and the proletarian dictatorship is its application, though Ho also called it a state of the whole people.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not discussed in any source; the conspiracy theory is foreign to an ideology that explains oppression through colonialism and class.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; elections were held in 1946 but the electoral system was not a theme.

national-mission.rationale: Ho supported solidarity with other socialist parties but each party takes its own road; exporting a form of government is not the goal.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Ho wrote of women as especially exploited under colonialism and the Party promoted equality; structural patriarchy as a thesis is inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Ho attacked corruption and urged a clean, strong party, but adherents defend their own leaders; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Implied by the Declaration's claim that all peoples are equal from birth; eugenic restrictions are not discussed in the sources.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology defends its armed forces while valuing party self-criticism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state leads economy, culture and education in socialism.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Implied by Ho's attacks on colonial racial division and the Declaration's equality of peoples; intermarriage is not discussed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration states that all the peoples on earth are equal from birth with the right to live, be happy and free.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Ho built socialism in the North while supporting world movement; the Party held socialism could be built in one country and ties it to the international struggle.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Ho condemned colonial settlement displacing peasants from land, supporting the characterization.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equality before the law for all is implied, but not discussed directly.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Ho spoke well of Christianity and religions; conversion restriction is not part of the ideology.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No tradition in Vietnamese communism of cattle protection, working animals aside; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Party is secular and education is state-controlled; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Ho praised the Soviet-led socialist camp and the strengthening of socialist states against imperialist plots.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Declaration claims the government represents the whole Vietnamese people, and the ideology says people are masters, but authority is also vested in the Party.

trade-surplus.rationale: Ho's writings do not discuss trade balances, and the doctrine gives no basis for a position.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts equality of peoples and ethnic unity in the ideology.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Ho urged the Comintern to help colonial peasants to insurrection and revolution, accepting force against the colonial order rather than only in self-defense.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Implied by the Marxist-Leninist emphasis on solidarity and on unity of workers, peasants and intellectuals; competition between peoples is not discussed.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: A Party-led state would outlaw parties seeking to overturn it; inferred from one-party leadership.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The Declaration condemns being subject to foreign arbitrary rule; the republican idea is not an explicit theme, so inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The Party leads all state organs under democratic centralism rather than checks among separate bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Party is the center of the revolution and the core of the national liberation movement, as in Leninism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The ideology's aims are liberation of workers and peasants and improving the material life of the people.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed in Ho's writings; a Western policy with no counterpart in the doctrine.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; strikes under the Party-led state are not an issue the ideology treats.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Ho blamed colonial exploitation and landlords for peasant poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The ideology prizes unity among ethnic groups under equality; inferred from Ho's 1955 letter's spirit and the Party's policy.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Cadre selection is by Party under democratic centralism.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: A Party-led state in war or emergency would set aside normal protections to defeat enemies; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State-led economy implies price control of essentials; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Party leadership of ideology and propaganda is central to the ideology's practice.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armed forces are led by the Party, as in Leninist practice; building people's armed forces under Party leadership.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed in the doctrine, so no position can be derived.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Cadres should be modest and frugal servants of the people, which is consistent; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Ho cited Lenin on centralized organization and strict internal discipline and defended discipline alongside socialist democracy.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Independence and unity are core; pooling sovereignty with capitalist countries would be opposed, though socialist camp solidarity is welcome.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Party commands the army and the head of state is not independent of it; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not a political issue in the ideology.

clerical-rule.rationale: Implied by the Party's role as the center of the revolution and leader of the state, which leaves no place for clerical authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Ho applied Lenin's anti-imperialist line to colonial wars, but a patriot who put national defense first would not wish his own nation's defeat; inferred, not stated in the sources opened.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Culture serves the people's spiritual life and Party aims; Ho addressed artists in 1951, so some censorship is plausible but unconfirmed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Ho served as president continuously; no term limits in the DRV constitutions; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: People are masters and cadres are servants, supporting recall, though under Party management.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Ho praised the socialist camp and its solidarity, so he did not favor ending alliances, though he opposed imperialist bases.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not part of the ideology; socialist Vietnam used state housing.

people-in-arms.rationale: National defense by all people and a people's armed forces; Ho kept a regular army as well, so not a full replacement.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Peasants are the revolutionary vanguard in pre-industrial society but the aim is to narrow the town-country gap, not romanticize rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National unity and independence were Ho's central aims; Vietnam's division by the 1954 settlement was to be undone.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Intellectuals are part of the united worker front, but cadres are also warned against detachment; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Declaration affirms equality of all peoples, but a civilizational hierarchy is not discussed; Ho criticized colonial claims of high civilization.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; the DRV applied capital punishment to traitors and criminals; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Ho's writings do not address sex education, and no position can be derived from them.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The materialist, scientific outlook of Marxism-Leninism rejects teaching creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Revolutionary morality and Party control of culture suggest restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not addressed in Ho's texts or the Party's formulation of his thought.

minority-language-support.rationale: Ho's 1955 letter to the Thai-Meo Autonomous Region reflects equality for minority peoples; inferred for languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law for religious minorities are not covered by the doctrine.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Revolutionary morality emphasizes collective discipline and modest conformity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The Declaration condemns colonial exploitation, supporting a view that colonial debts are illegitimate; not stated for current debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ho held that national liberation must lead to socialism, ending colonial economic exploitation and landlordism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1945 government planned a general election for an assembly, and the 1946 election produced the first constitution.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Party-led development justified temporary limits, inferred from the dictatorship of the proletariat doctrine.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Ho valued international aid and cooperation among socialist countries; for wealthy capitalist countries it is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The DRV president was chosen by the National Assembly; not an ideological issue.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Under state-led economics banks serve state plans.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: National unity is central, but Ho negotiated settlements including the 1954 partition; split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property exists in transition but ownership by workers and the state is the goal, subordinated to the people's interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Ho praised the Soviet Union as leading the socialist camp.

collective-defense.rationale: Ho stressed solidarity among socialist states against imperialism; mutual defense is consistent.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Ho held that Vietnam under French or Japanese power was not freely consenting; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Party-state asserts civil authority over institutions, though Ho spoke respectfully of religion; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ho himself led the Party and the state; the head of state was not above the Party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: National unity and independence are core and the Party-state would defend them by force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; Vietnam's ethnic autonomous regions existed, but a distinct economic system was not raised.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Declaration celebrates ending the monarchy; a divine ruler is rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Equality and fair relations favor progressive taxation; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxism-Leninism sees consciousness shaped by social conditions, and Ho's morality program assumes character can be trained.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration says the people hold the power and the state is of the people; a ruler above the law is rejected.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The ideology gives power to the people under the Party, not a balance of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Ho criticized the cult of personality as a defect and praised its Soviet critique, though Ho himself became revered; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are outside anything the doctrine addresses.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought discusses contradictions in transition, but the Maoist thesis that party leaders may restore capitalism is not his.

land-redistribution.rationale: Ho denounced colonial land concentration and the DRV carried out land reform giving land to cultivators.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not a theme of the doctrine, so no position is derived.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The ideology is anti-imperialist and focuses on Vietnam's own territory; not addressed directly.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the secular Party state, which never made religious law binding.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the Party's secular rule and its commitment to women's equality.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not addressed by the doctrine or by Ho's writings.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed; solidarity was among socialist parties.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Ethnic minorities received autonomous regions, but the statement concerns schools and institutions; not addressed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration versus local struggle is not addressed by Ho Chi Minh Thought.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is the foundation, which makes productive forces and relations decisive; Ho's own stress on national will tempers it.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; state socialism subsumes the question.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm bailouts are not discussed; the doctrine gives no direct basis for an answer.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women's equality was promoted, but quotas were not discussed in the sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Ho emphasized cooperation with the socialist camp and international aid rather than closed blocs.

moral-incentives.rationale: Party members are taught industriousness, thrift, integrity and selflessness, but no source says moral incentives should replace material ones, and socialist distribution stayed according to labor.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Ho's approach rests on Party organization and mass movement ripening, not focoist armed groups manufacturing conditions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Declaration ends the monarchy and proclaims equality from birth.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The ideology draws on national tradition; inferred for education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Ho mocked the so-called civilizing mission in his writings and demanded independence.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotism is central, and morality is part of mandatory school education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Equality and correcting oppression suggest opposition; not directly addressed.

public-money-creation.rationale: State control of the economy implies public money creation; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Following Lenin, imperialism produces crises and colonial revolution; adherents doubt it can avoid collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Ho demanded breaking all colonial relations with France.

delink-world-market.rationale: Ho wanted aid and cooperation with the socialist camp rather than complete delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Ho urged Western Communist parties to support colonial peoples, but did not adopt the labor aristocracy thesis explicitly.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Implied by the Declaration's equality of all peoples from birth; the private right to refuse service is not discussed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1946 constitution had a bill of rights, but entrenchment against majorities is not a theme.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The Declaration repudiates colonial relations and treaties with France.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Declaration founds a republic by popular authority, replacing the monarchy.

minority-veto.rationale: Discipline binds party members to decisions once adopted under democratic centralism.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Declaration justifies uprising against oppressive rule that violates people's rights.

parliament-supreme.rationale: National Assembly was formally supreme in the DRV constitution, but the Party leads it; not a stated principle.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare does not appear in the doctrine or in Ho's writings.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The use of animals for food or research is not addressed by the doctrine.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Cadres serve the people, but the ideology frames this as class liberation rather than noblesse oblige.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ho demanded public-spiritedness and active service to the nation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; culture is seen as serving the Party's aims.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Ho saw colonial rule as sustained by propaganda in the mother country, a partial echo of this view, but no explicit hegemony theory.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Ho described colonial peoples as unremittingly exploited by imperialist capital.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for native-born citizens is not addressed by the doctrine.

party-own-road.rationale: Ho argued that national features and conditions peculiar to each country become more important in shaping a party's policy, within Marxism-Leninism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Ho stressed learning from other socialist countries and using international aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Demands for lost territory are not part of the doctrine, which centers on Vietnam's own independence.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The Party leads regardless of origin; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Ho's movement fought Japanese fascists; inferred as consistent.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Implied: a communist doctrine that fought fascist Japan and calls itself a people's democracy rejects being equated with fascism; the sources do not address the comparison.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A question of American historiography that Ho Chi Minh Thought does not address.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Debates over contested monuments do not arise in the doctrine, so no position is derived.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Programs for boys and men are not addressed by the doctrine or Ho's writings.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not addressed by Ho Chi Minh Thought.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Ho argued national features and conditions peculiar to each country shape the road to socialism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army serves under Party leadership and does not stand as an independent guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Paying for domestic labor is not discussed by Ho or the Party's formulation of his thought.

filial-duty.rationale: Ho criticized Confucian ethics but kept parts of its self-cultivation; split and candidate.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; cadres were selected by the Party, with Confucian meritocracy criticized by Ho.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: State-led economy with a leading state sector implies blocking foreign control of strategic industries.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not addressed in the doctrine, so no position can be derived.

recallable-delegates.rationale: People are masters and cadres their servants, but binding mandates under democratic centralism are not stressed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State and collective provision rather than private accounts is the socialist norm.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Ho denounced the end of collective ownership under colonialism, but land policy gave land to tillers, not tenure by use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not a theme of the doctrine, which stresses Party leadership of the state.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred: Ho's declaration stresses equality of peoples and the DRV promoted minority-language education alongside Vietnamese, though Vietnamese was the common state language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Ho's focus on land for the peasantry and ending colonial exploitation of Vietnamese land.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; Ho stresses equality of peoples and classes but the outcome-based test is a modern Western legal idea.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The doctrine's ethic calls on cadres and people to be thrifty and frugal, and socialism is set against bourgeois acquisitiveness.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from Ho's proletarian internationalism and the Comintern duty to aid colonial liberation struggles, which the DRV later practiced in Laos and Cambodia.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Ho's 1956 article stresses national roads to socialism and equality among parties, which tells against forced intervention, though loyalty to the Soviet camp was strong; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist critique of capitalist control of the state, though the sources do not discuss lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's anti-colonial stress on national independence and the one-party state's wariness of outside interference.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from Vietnamese state population policy; the sources do not address it directly.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no settled position on local residency limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: Socialism under the Party aims at work for all in a state-led economy; inferred from the state-sector emphasis.

democratic-peace.rationale: The doctrine sees imperialist powers waging war under liberal-democratic banners and stresses the class character of states, so it doubts that spreading democracy brings peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The doctrine demands discipline and obedience to the Party and state law; inferred from the 1956 article on ideological unity.

non-intervention.rationale: Split: the 1945 Declaration asserts Vietnam's sovereignty against foreign rule, but the doctrine backed other liberation movements and the DRV aided the Pathet Lao and Khmer insurgents, so intervention 'for any reason' was not ruled out.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist labour organisation; the sources do not discuss craft versus industrial unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, which grounds enmity in imperialism and class rather than a minority; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's Confucian-influenced stress on family; marriage is retained as a state-regulated institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Party-led state controls information; adherents have no stated position on a legal right of access, so neutral.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national economic independence and self-reliance.

informal-organisation.rationale: The doctrine requires organisation under a permanent, disciplined Marxist-Leninist party; the 1956 article stresses Party unity.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The doctrine insists on national sovereignty but the state also joins international communist and legal bodies; adherents are not settled on this.

religious-nation.rationale: The doctrine is secular Marxism-Leninism that treats national identity as a political and cultural community, not a religious one.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The 1945 Declaration asserts the equality of peoples and national independence, and Ho opposed tribute-style subordination.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought stresses national unity and a strong state sector pooling resources; inferred, as regional revenue is not addressed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxism-Leninism leaves personal property private while production is held in common; inferred, as not a theme in the sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: Ho was a communist who built the Soviet-aligned socialist camp's unity, so defeating communism is rejected.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The doctrine stresses a strong state sector and state leadership of the economy; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist-Leninist materialism treats religion as a product of social conditions; inferred, though Ho practised religious tolerance.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Ho stressed capitalism's colonial exploitation and aimed for socialism without a capitalist stage; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ho backed women's equality as part of the socialist revolution; inferred from the doctrine's aims.

socialized-care.rationale: Socialist construction aims at collective provision for the people; inferred, as not a theme in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purity is not addressed in the sources; inferred as not part of the doctrine.

treaties-binding.rationale: The 1945 Declaration promises equality among peoples, which an adherent would extend to ethnic minorities' agreements; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The doctrine is built around a Party-led nation-state, not small autonomous communes; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: The doctrine stresses unity among ethnic groups but does not address majority settlement; adherents split, inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ho held socialism to be the path, with capitalism and imperialism the enemy, so a third way is rejected; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: Ho's 1945 Declaration of Independence asserts Vietnam's right to the land on grounds of the Vietnamese people's own history and struggle, but the sources do not frame it as a priority over other residents.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Ho's anti-fascist stance in the Declaration and the Comintern reports opposes Nazism; denial is inferred to be foreign to it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address it and the Party has not criminalized it, but Party morality was conservative.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Ho Thought holds that the Communist Party leads the state, and the DRV in Ho's lifetime did not tolerate organized opposition parties.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: the sources present Ho Thought as secular Marxism-Leninism, so the state punishing blasphemy has no basis, though it also did not promote religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Ho's 1924 report and 1945 Declaration condemn French colonial exploitation of Vietnam for French benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: Ho Thought calls for armed resistance to foreign invasion on national grounds and has no religious duty framing.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Ho Thought is secular and revolutionary, but it removes rulers for colonial or class reasons, not for failing to follow religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: Ho Thought stresses a state of the people with mass participation, but under Party leadership rather than direct decision-making in workplaces and universities.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: Ho linked colonial, class and women's oppression in his Comintern report, though not in terms of an intersecting framework.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred: not addressed in the sources, and the DRV era and Party tradition are socially conservative on this question.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Ho Thought is a Marxist-Leninist class framework, and the 1956 article stresses ideological unity of Marxist-Leninist parties, which rejects blending left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Ho Thought is based on Marxism-Leninism and condemns capitalist and colonial exploitation of workers and peasants, though alienation as a term is not featured.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: Ho's anti-colonial and internationalist stance rejects racial or civilizational hierarchies, though the sources do not address Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Ho Thought is atheist-materialist Marxism-Leninism and places authority in the people as led by the Party, as the Declaration invokes the people's rights.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: Ho Thought is secular but the DRV under Ho tolerated religion, so it has no clear position on dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: not addressed in the sources, and it is anachronistic for the DRV period.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ho Thought as scoped here aims at a socialist, state-led economy; the market-oriented Doi Moi line is excluded by the scope.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Ho Thought is built on armed national liberation, and the 1945 Declaration commits the nation to resist with all its force.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: Ho Thought stresses equality and collective ownership, which cuts against letting some grow rich first, a line associated with later Doi Moi reforms.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: Ho aligned with the Comintern and the socialist camp and the 1956 article stresses unity among Marxist-Leninist parties, but also stressed national independence.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The 1945 Declaration of Independence ended monarchy and founded a republic of the people, so hereditary succession is rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from the preference for state and collective economic ownership and cooperatives; no credit scheme is stated.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and the stress on national economic independence; the sources do not discuss international lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: The state is described as of the people, based on workers and peasants, and the Declaration claims universal rights.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ho supported women's liberation alongside national liberation; the nature link is inferred.

reification.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is the ideology's foundation and its critique of capitalist relations is part of that; the specific term is not stated in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist view holds that bourgeois freedoms are formal under class rule, and Ho's writings criticise colonial capitalist control of institutions.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Declaration appeals to law and rights and the DRV adopted a constitution, but Party leadership above the legal order is also central; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Declaration affirms that all peoples are equal, and Ho's colonial-question report rejects racial hierarchy.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the emphasis on mass participation, though through Party-led channels.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: a Party-led state tends to control information, though Ho stressed cadres' accountability to the people.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's equal rights and Marxist secularism; no marriage policy is stated.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from the unity of all ethnic and religious groups under the national front.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: Ho Chi Minh Thought vests leadership in the Party and a state of the people through party-led organs, so lot-selected citizen bodies do not fit; not stated in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: Ho Chi Minh Thought is Marxist-Leninist and secular, treating doctrine as adaptable to national conditions; religion is not discussed directly in the cited sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ho's Marxist critique of colonial capital and landlords implies concentrated wealth is a danger to the people's independence and freedom; the liberty framing itself is inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Ho never addressed it; Marxist-Leninist orthodoxy of his era treated homosexuality as a bourgeois deviation, so an adherent would lean against, an inference.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Ho's DRV guaranteed freedom of belief and courted religious believers in the united front, so state-driven atheist education is not his line; inferred from that stance.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Ho's state is the people's democratic dictatorship led by the Party, which keeps the police and security organs as instruments of the revolution, not something to abolish.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Ho's united front gave minorities and other classes a place, but power rested with Party-led majority rule under democratic centralism, so formal communal power-sharing is inferred as unwelcome.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Ho favored a strong state sector and organized mass mobilization for relief and welfare rather than reliance on charity; inferred from his socialist program.

term-limits.rationale: Ho led until his death and the Party values continuity of proven leadership; term limits are not in his writings, so this is inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Ho's model is democratic centralism with Party leadership, not revocable delegated voting; inferred from his 1956 account of Party unity.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk as such was not part of his thought; adherents prize peace and national construction but no stated priority exists.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Ho championed women's equality in all fields as a revolutionary aim; religious offices were not discussed, so this is inferred from the general principle.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Ho's program of women's emancipation and equality in the family implies shared marital authority rather than husband's rule.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the emphasis on a state of the people and national sovereignty after colonial rule.

rent-control.rationale: Not in the sources; inferred from the commitment to a strong state sector and an economy serving the working people.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist-Leninist opposition to private monopoly points one way, state interest in science and culture the other.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Ho's movement organised youth into Party-led groups such as the Youth Union and Pioneers, to train them for national tasks.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not stated; inferred from anti-imperialist opposition to the great-power military presence on Vietnamese soil.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Ho's anti-colonial struggle aimed at expelling foreign armies and securing full independence from imperial powers.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Ho's texts denounce colonial massacres, so recognition is consistent with them, but the issue itself is not addressed; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marxism-Leninism, which Ho adopted, treats rent and profit as exploitation and holds that income should come from labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Ho led armed struggle for independence and the Declaration of Independence pledges to resist colonial force to the end.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ho appealed to Vietnam's long history of resistance, but the sources do not say that the nation is continuous from antiquity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; Ho supported women's equality but did not treat sex categories as constructed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Ho treated women's liberation as part of a united class and national struggle, with women's unions organised under the Party; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The doctrine honours revolutionary martyrs and heroes of national liberation, though in a secular rather than saintly manner.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: As a Marxist-Leninist, Ho understood politics as class and national struggle on materialist grounds, not as a spiritual battle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Ho's aim was a unified Vietnam holding its people; diaspora centrality is not addressed.

culture-before-state.rationale: Ho put political independence and the Party-led state first, with culture to serve the revolution and national liberation.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; Ho's materialist ideology takes no stance on religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; atheist-materialist doctrine does not judge scripture by this standard.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ho's internationalism and class framing oppose economic privilege by nationality, though he stressed national economic independence; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; Ho's goal was national unity of Vietnam, but the sources do not discuss regions for peoples.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninist practice, in which unions work under Party leadership.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought makes the working class and peasantry the base of a state of the people led by the Party.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the strong state sector and the aim of serving the people's welfare.

second-chamber.rationale: The DRV used a single-chamber National Assembly; inferred from that and the Party-led state model.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from state and cooperative ownership in Marxism-Leninism rather than municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from democratic centralism and a unitary state under Party leadership.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the socialist aim of providing for workers' material needs.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources for a position.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed and anachronistic; no basis in the sources for a position.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from state economic control and Party oversight under Marxism-Leninism.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Party-state control of communication.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the collectivist Marxist-Leninist subordination of the individual to the nation and Party.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Socialism is described as improving the people's material and spiritual life.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the unitary state that Ho's national unity project aimed at.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state-led development and food security aims.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no basis in the sources for a position.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the class-based and internationalist framing, which rejects racial political organisation.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; national pride was central but racial pride is not discussed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Ho's movement waged armed struggle for independence and reunification, so it did not limit force to defence; inferred from that record.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: Ho's Declaration treats the Vietnamese as one people with a shared history and territory but also stresses equality of all peoples, and neither source defines nation by language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: the Party's unity of all people under a single state and secular line cuts against separate religious electorates, which colonial rulers used to divide.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Ho's Declaration condemns the French for splitting Vietnam into three regions to wreck its unity, and the movement treats foreign division as a tool of imperialism.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: Ho's 1945 declaration condemns colonial neglect of schooling, and the DRV built mass education, but tuition is not discussed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the sources never address pollution or finite resources, and a strong state sector would use planning rather than pricing.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred: independence and socialism are framed as a legacy for later generations, but Earth stewardship is not discussed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: Ho promoted women's equality in the declaration but did not claim women bring distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: Ho's line calls for armed defense of the independent state and the Soviet camp, so general disarmament is not a priority.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: Ho condemned imperialist secret treaties and made the Declaration a public appeal to nations, but the Party's own diplomacy was not open.

capital-controls.rationale: Official Ho Chi Minh Thought gives a strong role to the state sector and denounces colonial exploitation, which implies state control over capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed directly; a Party-led state with a people's army suggests armed force belongs to the state, though people's war used militias; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Ho condemned imperialist war but defended wars of national liberation, so refusal applies to some wars only; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Under a planned socialist economy wages are set by the state and Party-led unions, not bargained freely; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; a state-planned economy would use direct provision and wages rather than tax credits; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; a state-led socialist economy would not accept legal limits on public borrowing; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The 1924 report on colonies denounces imperialist exploitation of colonised peoples and calls for their liberation and equal standing.

smash-state-machine.rationale: As a Marxist-Leninist, Ho held that the colonial and old state apparatus is to be replaced by a new people's state, as in the 1945 revolution.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Ho's socialism is a Marxist-Leninist project led by the Party along a set path, not a free experiment among communities.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; a state-led socialist economy has no tradition of pricing nature as capital; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Patriotism and national independence are central to the doctrine, which treats the nation's liberation as a supreme cause.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; a socialist state favouring the working people and youth would lean to relief; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Ho's anti-colonial analysis of exploitation of dependent peoples extends by analogy to unequal regions; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The 1945 Declaration invokes the universal rights to life, liberty and happiness, with all peoples born equal.

public-service-media.rationale: Marxist-Leninist practice makes the press a tool of the Party, so media free of government control is not accepted; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marxist-Leninist materialism holds no religion is the underlying truth, though the line tolerated belief; inferred from the ideology's principles.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Fifth Comintern report makes the peasantry a base and calls for land and relief from exploiters, so state or cooperative support for farmers fits; farm prices are not discussed.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; the Soviet camp line defended its deterrent while backing disarmament, and Ho wrote nothing on it, so adherents are split.

workers-own-party.rationale: The ideology insists the Party leads as the vanguard of the working class and peasantry, which is a party of their own.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the socialist aim of women's equality and liberation from feudal custom.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Ho's advocacy of women's equality and the 1945 Declaration's equality principle, though inheritance is not mentioned.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the ideology's emphasis on national unity of a single people.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the ideology's state-led economy, which leaves pollution to central rules or planning, not private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's end of monarchy and its popular authority, which leaves no formal place for hereditary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the ideology's collective, state-led ethic that puts the common good over individual liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the party-state's firm stance on crime; sentencing rules are not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national unity and a common national language; not directly addressed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Unions and other mass organisations were led by the Party in the DRV, so voluntary membership was not a central principle; inferred from that Party-led model.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification was not an issue in the sources; the DRV held elections but no position on ID can be drawn from Ho's texts.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1945 Declaration affirms equality of peoples and the DRV guaranteed freedom of religion, so no interpretation was meant to be privileged; inferred from that.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Ho Thought aims at a state of the people under Party leadership and the dictatorship of the proletariat, so democracy is judged by substance, not election procedure.

premarital-sex.rationale: Ho preached frugal, disciplined revolutionary morality but also women's liberation from feudal marriage; the sources do not settle premarital sex.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed in Ho's era; inferred from the Party's insistence on controlling information and public order.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the strong state sector and state-run provision of welfare, which favours separate state programmes over a single cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: The DRV gave women equal political rights in 1945-46, and Ho's anti-feudal programme included equality of women with men.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marxism-Leninism blames feudal and religious custom, but Ho was conciliatory toward religion and stressed feudal Confucian family order; adherents are split.

race-social-construct.rationale: The Declaration's equality of peoples and Ho's anti-colonial critique of racial hierarchy imply races are not natural divisions; inferred, not stated.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from Party-led mass organisations such as the Women's Union and the commitment to women's equality.

missingStatements.text: Genuine patriotism cannot be separated from internationalism among working people of all countries.
missingStatements.rationale: Ho states that genuine patriotism can never be separated from proletarian internationalism, and builds the whole doctrine on that link.

missingStatements.text: Public officials should live modestly and serve the people, practicing thrift, integrity and selflessness.
missingStatements.rationale: Cadres are to be leaders and loyal servants of the people and are taught industriousness, thrift, integrity and public-spiritedness.

notes: Sources are largely official or Party-affiliated; Ho's own texts rarely treat modern issues such as gender, drugs or environment, so many answers are inferred. Adherents in practice differ on market reform.
